issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or loses reverse
issues.sym: The Jimmy hesitates or revs up between gears, slips in first or second, shifts late or harshly, or won't back up at all. A transmission that worked fine when cold may start slipping once it warms up.
issues.why: The 4L60-E four-speed automatic used in the Jimmy wears internally with age, heat and towing. Common failure points include the reverse input clutch, worn clutch packs and a cracked or worn rear sun shell, which cause slipping and loss of gears.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell with the engine running and warm. Burnt, dark fluid or metal in the pan means internal wear. Avoid towing or hard acceleration and get a transmission shop diagnosis; a rebuild or a remanufactured unit is the usual fix.

issues.t: Intake manifold gaskets leak coolant
issues.sym: The coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle under the truck, or you see coolant crust near the top of the engine. In bad cases the oil looks milky or the engine overheats.
issues.why: The 4.3L Vortec uses intake manifold gaskets with plastic carriers that break down from DEX-COOL coolant and heat cycles. Coolant then seeps out externally or into the engine oil, which can ruin the bearings if ignored.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and check the oil dipstick for a milky look. Have the gaskets replaced with improved metal-frame versions soon, and change the oil afterward if coolant got into it.

issues.t: Rough running from the central 'spider' fuel injector
issues.sym: The engine runs rough or shakes at idle, misfires, or the check engine light comes on with misfire codes. You may notice a fuel smell or a long crank after the truck has sat.
issues.why: This engine feeds all six cylinders from one central injector unit with thin lines (the 'spider'). The poppet nozzles stick or leak with age, so some cylinders get too little or too much fuel.
issues.next: Have a shop read the misfire codes and test fuel pressure and leak-down. If the spider injector is at fault, replace it with the updated multi-port style unit, which fixes the problem for good.

issues.t: Fuel pump fails and engine won't start
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't fire, sputters at highway speed, or stalls and won't restart. You may not hear the usual hum from the fuel tank when you turn the key on.
issues.why: The in-tank electric fuel pump wears out, often around 100,000 miles. A clogged fuel filter makes the pump work harder and shortens its life.
issues.next: Have the fuel pressure tested before replacing parts. If the pump is weak, replace the pump module and the fuel filter together, and change the filter about every 30,000 miles after that.

issues.t: Front ball joints wear out
issues.sym: Clunking or popping from the front end over bumps, wandering steering, or uneven wear on the front tires.
issues.why: The Jimmy's front ball joints carry a lot of weight and wear out, especially on 4x4 trucks. A badly worn joint can separate and let the wheel fold under.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play at your next tire rotation or sooner if it clunks. Replace worn ball joints promptly and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: ABS light on from failed brake control module
issues.sym: The ABS warning light stays on. The regular brakes still work, but the anti-lock system is switched off, so the wheels can lock on slippery roads.
issues.why: The electronic brake control module that runs the ABS fails internally on these trucks. A bad wheel speed sensor or corroded wiring can cause the same light.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read so you don't replace the wrong part. A rebuilt module is a common fix; drive carefully in rain and snow until it's repaired.

issues.t: Misfire from worn distributor cap and rotor
issues.sym: Rough idle, stumbling under acceleration, and a flashing or steady check engine light, often worse in damp weather.
issues.why: The 4.3L still uses a distributor. The cap and rotor wear and build up carbon tracks, and a loose rotor screw can damage the cap, so spark jumps to the wrong place.
issues.next: Replace the cap and rotor (and the plug wires if they are old) with good-quality parts. It's a simple repair that often clears misfires on these engines.

issues.t: Dashboard gauges stick or stop working
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel, temperature or tach needle freezes, drops to zero or reads wrong, sometimes only now and then.
issues.why: The tiny stepper motors that move the gauge needles in this instrument cluster wear out. It's a common problem across GM's 1998-and-later small trucks and SUVs.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. A cluster repair shop can replace the gauge motors instead of the whole cluster. Don't rely on a stuck temperature or fuel gauge in the meantime.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge reads empty on a full tank, sticks at one level, or swings around while you drive.
issues.why: The fuel level sender in the tank wears where its contact rubs, or the gauge motor in the cluster fails.
issues.next: Track your fill-ups with the trip meter so you don't run out. A shop can tell whether the sender or the gauge is at fault; the sender is part of the fuel pump module.

issues.t: Air conditioning stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm or only cools some of the time, and you may hear the compressor clutch clicking on and off.
issues.why: Owners report A/C compressor and component failures at around 60,000 miles. Leaks at hoses and the condenser also let refrigerant escape.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks with dye before recharging. If the compressor has failed, the shop should also replace the accumulator and flush the lines so debris doesn't ruin the new one.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hub fails
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed, a loose feeling in the steering, or the ABS light coming on.
issues.why: The sealed front hub bearings wear out, especially on 4x4 trucks. The ABS sensor is built into the hub, so a failing bearing can also set the ABS light.
issues.next: Have the front hubs checked for play and noise. Replace a worn hub before it gets loose, since a failed bearing can affect steering.

issues.t: Four-wheel drive won't engage or clunks out
issues.sym: The 4WD light flashes or the system won't shift into four-wheel drive, or it drops out of 4WD with a loud clunk.
issues.why: The push-button 4WD system depends on the transfer case shift motor, the front axle actuator and their wiring. These parts fail or corrode with age.
issues.next: Have the 4WD system scanned and the front axle actuator and transfer case motor tested. Don't rely on 4WD in snow until it's confirmed working.

issues.t: Brakes pulsate from warped front rotors
issues.sym: The brake pedal or steering wheel shakes when you slow down, especially from highway speed.
issues.why: The front rotors on these trucks wear unevenly and warp from heat, and owners filed many complaints about brake rotor problems for these years.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Replacing them with quality rotors and pads, and torquing the wheels properly, usually cures the shake.

issues.t: Heater fan works only on some speeds
issues.sym: The blower works on high but not on the lower settings, or it quits altogether.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor burns out, often because an aging blower motor draws too much current.
issues.next: Replace the resistor, and the blower motor too if it's noisy or slow. It's a quick job behind the glove box area.

issues.t: Oil pressure gauge drops or jumps around
issues.sym: The oil pressure gauge falls to zero or swings around while the engine sounds normal.
issues.why: The oil pressure sending unit at the back of the engine fails or leaks. Real low oil pressure is much less common, but it must be ruled out.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. If the engine is quiet and full of oil, have a mechanical gauge test done; if pressure is fine, replace the sender.

issues.t: Doors sag and are hard to close
issues.sym: The doors drop when opened, rub or pop as they latch, and need to be lifted or slammed to close.
issues.why: The door hinge pins and bushings wear out on these trucks, especially on the heavier driver's door.
issues.next: Install a hinge pin and bushing kit. It's a simple repair and stops further wear on the striker and latch.

issues.t: Long crank before the engine starts
issues.sym: The engine turns over for several seconds before it starts, especially the first start of the day.
issues.why: Fuel pressure bleeds off overnight, often through a leaking spider injector or a weak check valve in the fuel pump, so the system has to build pressure again before the engine fires.
issues.next: Try turning the key to on for a few seconds before cranking. If that helps, ask a shop to run a fuel pressure leak-down test to find the leak.

issues.t: Upper ball joint can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end or loose steering; in the worst case the front suspension can collapse.
issues.why: GM recalled some 4x4 trucks because the upper control arm ball joint could separate.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a GMC dealer. If the recall wasn't done, the dealer will fix it free.

issues.t: Brake lights and hazards can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The brake lights or rear hazard flashers stop working, so drivers behind you get no warning when you slow down.
issues.why: A fault in the turn signal (multifunction) switch can cut power to the brake and hazard lamps. GM recalled the trucks, then recalled some again in 2008.
issues.next: Have someone watch the brake lights while you press the pedal. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer repair is free.

issues.t: Seat belt buckles may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the buckle may seem latched but not hold properly in a crash.
issues.why: Some TRW-made buckles did not meet the federal seat belt standard, so GM recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the buckles replaced free at a GMC dealer if needed.

issues.t: Seat belt webbing may tear (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign before a crash; the belt webbing could separate in a second impact or rollover.
issues.why: GM recalled these trucks because the seat belt webbing could be cut or separate during a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer will inspect and replace the belts free.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can quit (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers work on and off or stop completely, sometimes in the middle of a rainstorm.
issues.why: GM issued two recalls on these trucks for wiper motor and wiring faults that could stop the wipers.
issues.next: If your wipers act up, pull over when it's safe. Check your VIN for open recalls; the repair is free.

issues.t: Fuel system may leak in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning sign. Any raw fuel smell around the truck should be checked right away.
issues.why: GM recalled some 1996 trucks because the fuel system did not meet the federal crash fuel-leak standard, raising fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you smell fuel, don't drive the truck until it's inspected.

issues.t: Anti-lock brakes can lengthen stops (recall)
issues.sym: During a hard stop on mixed or rough surfaces, the truck takes longer to stop than expected.
issues.why: GM recalled these trucks after the ABS system was found to extend stopping distances in some hard-braking situations.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the repair is free. Leave extra following distance in the meantime.

issues.t: Power mirror switch can overheat in the door (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the driver's door, or a mirror switch that gets hot.
issues.why: GM recalled these trucks because the power mirror switch could short and overheat, possibly starting a fire in the door.
issues.next: If you smell burning from the door, stop and get out. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer fix is free.

issues.t: Driver seat belt may let out too much slack in a rollover (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the problem only shows up in a severe rollover crash.
issues.why: An energy-absorbing loop in the driver belt buckle could fully pay out in a multiple-rollover crash, so GM recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer will replace the buckle free.

issues.t: Brake hose or lower control arm defect (recalls)
issues.sym: A soft brake pedal or brake fluid leak, or a clunk or vague handling from the front suspension.
issues.why: GM issued two small recalls on 1998 trucks: one for a brake hose that could leak and one for a front lower control arm problem that could affect control.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls; both repairs are free at a GMC dealer.

issues.t: Brake system seal can leak fluid (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels soft or sinks, the brake warning light may come on, and stops take longer.
issues.why: A seal in the brake system could break during assembly or from road and fluid-pressure cycles, letting brake fluid leak. GM recalled a small number of trucks.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. If the pedal feels soft, have the brakes checked before driving further. Check your VIN for open recalls.
